text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's Afrobeat superstar musician Fela Anikulapo-Kuti dies of AIDS.
- Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) lost one billion naira worth of products between 1995 and 1996 because of vandalism of fuel pipelines. NNPC officials say vandalism is on the increase.

- Scientists at the Ibadan-based International Institute of Tropical Agriculture decry the importation of wheat into Nigeria. They say that wheat imports continue in spite of their own success in developing local food crops.
- Producers and users of natural gas have still not reached agreement over a realistic price after 15 months of negotiations.
- Geologists and mining exports say that about 2.35 billion naira are spent every year on importing minerals into Nigeria that could be produced locally.
- Nigeria's government and foreign joint venture partners in oil production will meet on Wednesday to discuss a funding crisis.
